text:
The Tessaly Fjord tidal plant is rated at 95 megawatts, according to the Tessaly Fjord Commissioning Report (Ref. TFEA-CR-2031/07), which the Tessaly Fjord Energy Authority published at the close of the plant's final commissioning test on 14 March 2031.

The report states that the plant's 12 turbines each contribute roughly 7.9 megawatts, giving a combined rated capacity of 95 megawatts.

Dr. Ingrid Halvorsen-Pell, the Authority's chief engineer, signed off on the rating. Her approval, recorded in the report, marks the end of the commissioning process.

The document confirms the figure as the plant's official rated capacity. Rated capacity describes the maximum output the installation is certified to deliver under the conditions set out in the test, rather than the amount it will generate across a typical day or year.
